Which Hyalella lineages are our Atacama amphipods?

And where do their closest known relatives live?

We compared 30 PCR and 10 genome cox1 sequences with 3,109 public Hyalella records from NCBI and BOLD.

Five headline findings

  • 21 of 30 PCR samples are Andean Hyalella. Most belong to one unnamed high-Andean lineage known from the Argentine Puna and Antofagasta, Chile; 3 sit near Lake Titicaca species.
  • All 10 genome-derived cox1 are North American H. azteca. They are 99.4–99.8 % identical to haplotypes from eastern North America.
  • 9 PCR samples also point north. 5 match H. azteca (Canada, a French lab culture); 4 match a Nevada thermal-spring species.
  • No clear new species by barcode alone. Every sample is ≥ 97.2 % identical to a public sequence; 4 are borderline (< 98 %).
  • Before interpreting the northern matches, rule out contamination or sample mix-up. Atacama animals this close to North American and lab-culture lineages is not biologically expected.

Full explanation and caveats: report.md
